onboardingBody.message: StegoShard encrypts your file, then saves it in the form you pick. There are two families of output:

onboardingDeniable.message: Blends in as ordinary files — a set of photos, or a real-looking database. Pick this when the goal is to hide that a secret exists at all.

onboardingOvert.message: Openly StegoShard — QR images, a printable PDF, or a plain file. Pick this for a straightforward, resilient backup.

onboardingKeep.message: Either way, keep your password — there is no recovery if you lose it.

extraEntropyAlwaysCsprng.description: Reassurance shown next to the extra-entropy field: the CSPRNG is never replaced.

extraEntropyKeyHelp.message: This is the one place the vault key itself can be covered: it is created now, and entropy supplied later at save time cannot reach back to it. The key protects every vault you write on this device.
extraEntropyKeyHelp.description: Explanation under the extra-entropy field on the key-creation form: only here can the vault key itself be covered.

extraEntropyHelp.message: Whatever you type here is mixed (XORed) into every random value this save generates, on top of the browser's secure random generator — which is used regardless. It can only add uncertainty, never replace it, so a weak string cannot weaken your vault. It covers this save's salts, nonces and other generated values; a vault key already held in the key store was created earlier and is not affected. Nothing about it is stored: you never re-enter it to restore.
